title: Policy Translator: Natural-language to Batch/Cache Presets with Confidence Ribbons
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Operators struggle to map high-level goals (eg. minimize cost, maintain p95 latency, tolerate 1% quality drop) into safe batching and prefix/KV cache settings. Current presets are opaque and require infra knowledge.

Proposal: Design an in-console 'Policy Translator' that accepts natural-language operator intents and converts them into recommended batch/cache presets. The UI surfaces a confidence ribbon and inline tradeoff explainers (cost impact, latency distribution, risk of degradation) and allows quick one-click apply, simulate, or open advanced editor. The flow includes an optional conservative mode that injects guardrails (max batch size, KV cache TTL floor, fallback model variant).

Goals: 1) Reduce time-to-safe-configuration for new operators by 60% in lab tasks. 2) Improve uptake of recommendations vs default presets. 3) Provide transparent cost/latency/noise estimates for each recommendation.

Scope: Console-only prototype (Figma + interactive HTML mock), does not change runtime behavior. UX and copy for translator modal, confidence ribbon, explainers, simulation panel, and rollback CTA.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype with translator modal, confidence ribbon, and simulate panel in Figma linked and reviewed
Copy and microcopy approved by Content and PM
User test (5 operators) shows task completion < 5 minutes for configuring workload preset
Design handed off with tokens, states, and accessibility notes
Engineering implementation feasibility signoff from ENG infra and API teams
decisions: Translator will produce 3 ranked presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) with estimated token-cost delta and p50/p95 latency bands
Confidence ribbon uses green/amber/red with numeric confidence (0-100) computed from matching telemetry signatures
Simulation will run on historical anonymized traces (via a backend job) to surface expected impact without applying changes
Translator will surface both batch and KV-cache changes, but not quantization/precision toggles in v1
risks: Over-trusting translator recommendations could lead to regressions for niche workloads (mitigate via conservative default)
Estimations rely on representative traces; skewed traces produce bad guidance
Copy misunderstanding — users might think the translator is performing live changes; need clear disclaimers
